title: 雅努斯开启门后的沸泉
summary: 萨宾军逼近罗马，朱诺替来敌移开门闩，雅努斯便引出掺有硫黄的沸泉阻路。奥维德借神明自述，说明当地祭坛的来历，以及战时开门、和平关门的仪式含义。
paragraphs: 奥维德《岁时记》中，诗人询问雅努斯，为何他在罗马特定的门旁享有祭祀。神明回忆萨宾王塔提乌斯攻城之时，塔尔佩娅贪求臂饰，引导敌军登上堡垒。军队沿坡路走向谷地与广场，朱诺又把挡路的门闩移开，原本保护城市的通道突然向进攻者敞开。
雅努斯不愿与强大的朱诺正面争斗，转而运用自己掌管开合的力量。他先把硫黄放进水道，再开启泉口，让滚沸的水突然冲向来路。萨宾军不能穿过灼热的水流，被迫退下；危险解除以后，水泉恢复平常面貌，当地则为这次援助设立祭坛与小祠，以谷物和饼献祭。
诗人接着问，为何雅努斯的门在战争中打开、和平时反而关闭。神回答，开门为远征的民众留出归路，关门则让和平不要离去。这是奥维德公开讲述的城邦祭祀起源，不是关于私人幸运的泛泛寓言；沸泉解围与门的仪式相连，也不表示萨宾战争从此没有其他冲突。

en.title: Janus Opens the Boiling Springs
en.summary: When Juno unbars a Roman gate for the advancing Sabines, Janus opens another passage: springs made scalding with sulphur. Ovid connects this rescue to a local shrine and explains why the god’s doors open during war but close during peace.
paragraphs: In Ovid’s Fasti, the poet asks Janus why a particular Roman gateway belongs to his worship. The god recalls the attack of the Sabine king Tatius. Bribed with the promise of armlets, Tarpeia admitted enemies to the citadel. They descended toward the valley and forums, while Juno removed the bars of a gate that should have blocked their advance.

Unwilling to confront Juno directly, Janus used his own power over openings. He placed sulphur in the water channels, then opened the mouths of the springs. Scalding water rushed out and prevented the Sabines from passing. After the attackers were repulsed, the place returned to its ordinary appearance. A small shrine and altar commemorated the intervention with offerings of grain and cake.

The poet then asks why the god’s doors stand open during war and close during peace. Janus explains that departing citizens need an open road home, whereas closed doors keep peace from leaving. Ovid thus supplies a specific public narrative about a shrine and its ritual, not a general promise of personal luck or an account ending every Roman conflict.

title: 普罗塞耳皮娜与刻瑞斯的寻找
summary: 普罗塞耳皮娜被冥王掳走，刻瑞斯遍地寻女，使田野失去收成。朱庇特允诺归还，却因少女已吃冥界石榴而改为分居两界，此篇依奥维德的罗马改写叙述。
paragraphs: 在奥维德的《变形记》中，普罗塞耳皮娜在西西里采花，冥王狄斯突然驾车出现，把她强行带走。少女呼喊母亲，鲜花从衣襟散落，泉水女神库阿涅试图阻止，也没能拦下车辆。冥王以权杖裂开大地，带她进入地下；留在地上的母亲刻瑞斯并不知道女儿被带往何处。
刻瑞斯举着火炬走过各地，后来在泉水中发现女儿遗落的腰带，又从阿瑞图萨那里得知她已经身处冥界。愤怒的母亲让耕作失去成果，种子与田野不能继续供养人类。她向朱庇特要求归还女儿，得到附带条件的答复：只有少女尚未吃过冥界食物，才可完全返回地上。
然而普罗塞耳皮娜已在冥界吃下石榴籽，并有目击者作证。朱庇特于是安排她每年一半时间陪伴母亲，一半留在冥界，刻瑞斯才让大地重新结实。这里采用奥维德的平分年岁结局；它是罗马诗人接受希腊得墨忒耳故事的版本，不能拿别的传本种子数量推算所有叙述的月份。

en.title: Proserpina and the Search of Ceres
en.summary: Dis abducts Proserpina, and Ceres searches for her daughter while withholding the earth’s harvest. Jupiter permits a return, but food eaten below prevents a permanent reunion. Ovid’s Roman adaptation ends with the daughter dividing each year equally between two realms.
paragraphs: In Ovid’s Metamorphoses, Proserpina gathers flowers in Sicily when Dis appears in his chariot and carries her away. She calls for her mother as flowers fall from her clothing. The spring goddess Cyane attempts to stop the abduction, but cannot prevail. Dis strikes open a route beneath the earth, leaving Ceres without knowledge of where her daughter has gone.

Ceres searches widely with burning torches. Finding her daughter’s discarded belt and hearing Arethusa’s report, she learns that Proserpina is in the underworld. She prevents the land from producing its harvest and appeals to Jupiter for her child’s return. He makes full restoration conditional upon one requirement: the girl must not have eaten any food in the realm below.

Proserpina has already eaten pomegranate seeds, and a witness reports it. Jupiter therefore divides her year equally between her mother and the underworld; Ceres allows the earth to bear again. This follows Ovid’s Roman adaptation of Greek Demeter traditions. Its division should not be recalculated from seed counts borrowed from other tellings, as though every ancient account used one calendar.
